beads.title: KB: capture the real push+pr 'Resource not accessible by integration' entry and point the eval at it
beads.description:
Judge-2 N4 (C:\akhil\apra-fleet-driver\planning\v045\judges\pr-797-judge-2-2026-11-06.md). The eval case for the gh 'Resource not accessible by integration' error hits only an invented fixture entry (tests/fixtures/kb-recall-eval/extra-entries.json, id eval-real-memory-vcs-auth-explicit-access); no real KB entry existed, so members hitting the error got noise.

Why the criteria were revised (re-plan pass 2, verified this pass): the fleet-sprint engine runs the bible commit (kb_bible_commit on the kb_maintainer) only in the harvest and final-review phases (packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/phases/harvest.mjs, final-review.mjs), after develop ends. The reviewer can only return kb_promotions; it never commits the bible. So a task whose closure needs the entry in .fleet/kb-canonical.json cannot close in develop. The eval reads a pinned bible snapshot (tests/fixtures/kb-recall-eval/bible-snapshot.json, copied from .fleet/kb-canonical.json by scripts/gen-kb-recall-eval.mjs line ~46) plus extra-entries.json (loaded in tests/helpers/kb-recall-eval.ts ~line 163). The fix is therefore to carry the REAL entry (real id, real content from the KB) in extra-entries.json until harvest lands it in the bible, and make the generator skip it once it is there.

Rule content of the entry: gh 'Resource not accessible by integration' means the GitHub App token lacks access -- re-mint via provision_vcs_auth with git_access push+pr (push alone cannot create PRs or dispatch workflows); repos as full owner/repo names.

Earlier runs: entry 4f54d973-5627-49c3-903a-466695892a45 was captured INFERRED (see notes); run 3 reported it was not visible via kb_query from the doer session, so check first and recapture if needed.

Lane: kbfix-bible, streakOrder 1, before the model-enabled eval task (streakOrder 2) which edits the same eval files. Lane effort (2+2) x standard 10 = 40, below laneTargetEffort 60: no other open lane remains to merge with.

Expected files: scripts/gen-kb-recall-eval.mjs, tests/fixtures/kb-recall-eval/* (extra-entries.json, queries.json, enrichment.json), tests/knowledge/kb-recall-eval.test.ts. Do NOT hand-edit .fleet/kb-canonical.json. Scope estimate, not an allowlist.
beads.acceptance_criteria: REVISED (re-plan pass 2; supersedes the earlier criteria, which needed a bible commit that only runs in the harvest/final-review phase after develop, so the task could never close in develop -- 3 doer runs made no progress). 1. The real entry exists in the live KB as INFERRED: kb_query with error_text 'Resource not accessible by integration' returns the push+pr runbook entry (id 4f54d973-5627-49c3-903a-466695892a45, or a fresh capture if that id is not visible from the doer's session -- record the id used in notes). It carries the error text as an error_signature and evidence pointing at the provision_vcs_auth git_access docs/code. 2. The recall eval case for this error points at that real entry id, not the invented id eval-real-memory-vcs-auth-explicit-access: MISS_ENTRY_ID in scripts/gen-kb-recall-eval.mjs and tests/knowledge/kb-recall-eval.test.ts is the real id, and extra-entries.json holds the real entry (its id, title, summary, error_signatures and evidence exported from the KB with kb_export or kb_list, not hand-invented). 3. The generator adds that extra entry only when the id is NOT already in .fleet/kb-canonical.json, so once harvest commits the entry to the bible, regenerating the fixtures does not duplicate it (unit-check: run the generator twice; extra-entries.json is unchanged and no duplicate id appears across bible-snapshot.json and extra-entries.json). 4. A grep of the repo for eval-real-memory-vcs-auth-explicit-access returns no hits. 5. The recall eval passes through the npm test runner with its existing thresholds, and the keyword-only config ranks the real entry first for the error-text query. 6. Reviewer promotion to CONFIRMED and the bible commit are NOT closure conditions for this task: the reviewer judges the entry from its promotion-candidate block, and the harvest phase commits it. Close once 1-5 hold.

beads.description:

beads.title: [impl] Hybrid order guarantees every keyword top-5 hit a place in the top 8
beads.description:
Fixes judge-2 N3 (parent bug). Same lane as the N1 fix (kbfix-additive) because both edit SqliteProvider.hybridRows.

Problem: src/services/knowledge/hybrid-rank.ts reciprocalRankFusion + hybridOrder let semantic-backed rows overtake a keyword-only hit and push it out of the 8-entry pushed block. Judge example: query 'test isolation APRA_FLEET_DATA_DIR temp git repos MCP client HTTP transport' -- keyword rank 5, hybrid rank 10, semantic rank 47. The pushed block size is 8 (KB_MAX_KNOWLEDGE_ENTRIES in the engine).

Change: keep the hybrid (fused x trust prior) order, then apply a guard: every id in the keyword list's top 5 (that passed the filters) is guaranteed a position within the first 8 of the final order. Suggested shape: a pure helper in hybrid-rank.ts (e.g. guardKeywordTop(order, keywordTop, keep=5, within=8)) that, when a keyword top-5 id sits below position 8, moves it up to the lowest position inside the first 8, displacing the lowest-ranked non-guarded rows down, preserving relative order otherwise; call it in hybridRows on the order before slicing to limit. Export the 5 and 8 as named constants. When there is no keyword list (query without keyword terms, or keyword disabled via disable_lists) the guard is a no-op. Document the rule in the hybridRows doc comment (D2f additive rule).

Judge measurements for context (do not need to reproduce): real-42 R@5 0.976 -> 1.000, R@8 0.976 -> 1.000; real bible no cost.

Expected files: src/services/knowledge/hybrid-rank.ts, src/services/knowledge/sqlite-provider.ts (hybridRows call site). Scope estimate, not an allowlist.

Acceptance criteria:
- A pure function in hybrid-rank.ts implements the guard; with keyword top-5 ids all already in the first 8 it returns the input order unchanged.
- hybridRows applies it so, for any hybrid query with a keyword list and limit >= 8, each keyword top-5 id is in the returned rows.
- Order of rows that are not moved by the guard is otherwise unchanged (relative order preserved).
- Existing tests in tests/knowledge/kb-query-hybrid*.test.ts still pass (run via the repo npm test runner, targeted).

beads.title: [test] Bearer parsing and mini-dom parsing are linear and supervisor errors carry no stack trace
beads.description:
Regression tests for the CodeQL fixes in the preceding task of this lane (same lane, runs after it). Existing test file from the first round: packages/apra-fleet-se/test/codeql-hardening.test.mjs -- extend it rather than starting over.

REPLAN NOTE (review round 1): the old criterion that restoring /^Bearer\s+(.+)$/i must make the timing test fail is DROPPED. It cannot be met: the regex is anchored, header values cannot contain a newline, so .+$ always matches and there is no super-linear input. The timing test stays as a forward guard only. Also, the review found that the first stripStacks rework applied stripping to EVERY sendJson payload (success bodies included), truncating strings at a newline followed by at-word and dropping any key named stack, and used the backtracking regex /\r?\n\s*at\s+\S/. The preceding impl task is being reworked to strip stacks only on the error path with no backtracking regex; the tests below pin that corrected behaviour.

What to test:
(a) Bearer parsing, via checkMutatingRequest in packages/apra-fleet-workflow/src/viewer/request-guard.mjs: a valid token under each of Bearer, bearer and BEARER is accepted; an empty bearer value counts as no token; a hostile header (Bearer plus about 50k spaces with and without a trailing char) returns within a generous time bound.
(b) mini-dom: feed packages/apra-fleet-se/test/helpers/mini-dom.mjs a hostile open tag with a long attribute run and no closing >, and assert it finishes under the bound and does not throw.
(c) Supervisor error bodies carry no stack: a route handler that throws (500 keeps its fixed message), and at least the two named callers through their real HTTP routes -- the reconcile route 404 (packages/apra-fleet-se/src/supervisor/reconcile.mjs ~257, error built from err.message) and the id-allocator allocate 503 (packages/apra-fleet-se/src/supervisor/id-allocator.mjs ~563) -- where the underlying error carries a stack-bearing message. Assert no at-frame line and no path ending in .mjs:line in the body.
(d) Success payloads pass through unchanged: a success response sent through sendJson whose string field contains text like Keep cookies? newline at least one option must stay, and an object with a key named stack (e.g. {stack: node,react}), comes back byte-for-byte equal to JSON.stringify of the input.
(e) Linear time: whatever stack-stripping helper the impl task ends up with, fed an error message made of about 50k newlines (and a variant of 50k newline-plus-spaces with no at frame), returns within a generous bound (e.g. under 100ms).

Framework: whatever the neighbouring test file uses (node:test in apra-fleet-se). Run through npm test only.

Expected files (best-effort, not an allowlist): packages/apra-fleet-se/test/codeql-hardening.test.mjs; a helper or fixture for driving the reconcile/allocator routes if needed.
beads.acceptance_criteria:
1. Each case (a)-(e) has at least one test, and every test asserts an observable property: token accepted or refused; parse/strip time under the bound; error body has no at-frame lines or .mjs:line paths; success body equals the input exactly.
2. Case (c) exercises the reconcile 404 and the allocator 503 through their HTTP routes, not only sendJson called directly.
3. Case (d) fails against the first-round stripStacks (strip applied to every payload); case (e) fails or exceeds its bound against the /\r?\n\s*at\s+\S/ regex on 50k newlines. Check each locally once against the old code and record the result in the test file header comment.

beads.title: Fix the bearer-token regex, the mini-dom tag regex and stack-trace exposure flagged by CodeQL on PR 806
beads.description:
Bug: CodeQL raised 3 new alerts on PR 806 (verdict: pr806-rejudge.md, path in the parent bug).

(a) packages/apra-fleet-workflow/src/viewer/request-guard.mjs presentedToken (~line 56) uses /^Bearer\s+(.+)$/i on the Authorization header. CodeQL flags it as polynomial ReDoS: \s+ followed by (.+) can backtrack over runs of whitespace. Replace it with a parse that cannot backtrack, e.g. a case-insensitive prefix check on bearer plus a single whitespace char, then slice and trim, or a regex with no ambiguous adjacent quantifiers. Keep the behaviour: case-insensitive scheme, surrounding whitespace trimmed, empty token = no token.
(b) packages/apra-fleet-se/test/helpers/mini-dom.mjs (~137, test-only, severity high): the open-tag regex has nested quantifiers over the attribute list ((?:\s+[^\s=/>]+(?:\s*=\s*(...))?)*\s*), which allows exponential backtracking. Rewrite the attribute scan so it cannot backtrack catastrophically, e.g. a linear hand-rolled scanner or a regex whose alternatives are disjoint. Every viewer DOM test that uses mini-dom must still pass.
(c) packages/apra-fleet-se/src/supervisor/server.mjs sendJson (~line 135) is the sink of a stack-trace-exposure flow (medium). Find each caller whose payload can carry an Error, an err.stack or a raw err value (searched this pass: sendJson calls in src/supervisor that pass err.message include api.mjs ~1030, id-allocator.mjs ~539 and reconcile.mjs ~257; the request wrapper at server.mjs ~319 already sends a fixed message). Make error responses carry only a message string, never a stack. A central guard is acceptable (e.g. sendJson normalizes an Error or a stack-bearing value to its message), as long as the identified flow is cut.

CI note: whether CodeQL reports zero new alerts can only be checked in CI. This task is closed on the locally checkable criteria below; do not wait for CI.

Expected files (best-effort, not an allowlist): packages/apra-fleet-workflow/src/viewer/request-guard.mjs, packages/apra-fleet-se/test/helpers/mini-dom.mjs, packages/apra-fleet-se/src/supervisor/server.mjs and the callers found.
beads.acceptance_criteria:
1. presentedToken no longer uses a regex with adjacent ambiguous quantifiers. It still accepts Bearer, bearer and BEARER with surrounding whitespace, and ignores a scheme with an empty token.
2. The mini-dom open-tag/attribute parse is linear: a 50k-char hostile attribute string such as many spaces and = with no closing > parses in under 100ms.
3. No supervisor error response body contains a stack trace (no at-frame lines); 500s keep the fixed message.
4. All existing viewer DOM tests and supervisor-csrf-guard tests still pass.
5. npm test passes in packages/apra-fleet-workflow and packages/apra-fleet-se.

beads.title: Child-id allocator legacy seed can collide with a still-running legacy supervisor
beads.description: packages/apra-fleet-se/src/supervisor/id-allocator.mjs seedFromLegacy() copies a snapshot of the legacy ~/.apra-fleet/supervisor allocator file (high-water marks and the free pool) when FLEET_SE_DATA_DIR is set and the new file is missing. If a legacy supervisor (no FLEET_SE_DATA_DIR) keeps running against the same beads DB, both allocators mint from the same snapshot and can hand out the same child id. Reusing the copied free pool makes this more likely. Fix options: (1) seed only the high-water marks and drop the free pool; or (2) detect a live supervisor still holding the legacy file and refuse loudly, or log a warning. Add a test in supervisor-id-allocator-data-dir.test.mjs for the concurrent case.

beads.title: Child viewer refuses token-bearing POSTs with a misleading invalid token error
beads.description: packages/apra-fleet-workflow/src/viewer/index.mjs calls checkMutatingRequest with hostOpts that have no token, so the child viewer has no token. Any request carrying Authorization: Bearer or X-Fleet-Token gets 403 'invalid token', even with a valid FLEET_SUPERVISOR_TOKEN. The supervisor proxy strips these headers, so proxied requests work, but a direct client of the child viewer port gets an error that wrongly blames the token. Either pass FLEET_SUPERVISOR_TOKEN through to the child viewer, or say clearly that the child viewer accepts no token. Add a case to supervisor-csrf-guard.test.mjs or the viewer tests.

beads.title: [test] Paused sprint resumes after an out-of-process bd human respond answer with real bd
beads.description:
End-to-end guard for the bug fix in the preceding task of this lane (pause-exempt periodic read of the decision bead while paused awaiting a decision).

What to test: build a real beads sandbox with real bd (follow the existing real-bd fixtures: packages/apra-fleet-se/test/helpers/beads-fixture.mjs and the real-bd tests such as test/child-floor-includes-closed-children.test.mjs). Then, out of process (a separate bd child process, not recordDecisionAnswer), run bd human respond on the decision bead. Use a short read-poll override via the env var or option the impl task adds, so the test runs in seconds.

Framework: node --test or vitest, matching the neighbouring decision tests in packages/apra-fleet-se/test. Run through npm test only (CLAUDE.md), never vitest/node --test directly.
beads.acceptance_criteria:
1. The run leaves paused-awaiting-decision and resumes after an answer is recorded by a separate bd human respond process. No in-process answer is queued and no operator Resume is issued.
2. After the resume, the work bead notes contain the answer text, and the decision is moved from pendingDecisions to answeredDecisions.
3. While waiting, the recorded command list contains no member release, re-reserve, resync, beads pull or pause/resume: only the periodic bd show reads (and bd comments after the bead closes).

beads.title: Detect a bd human respond answer while paused awaiting a decision and resume the sprint
beads.description:
Bug: while a sprint is paused-awaiting-decision, holdUntilReleased in packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/decision-wait.mjs (~452-488) only checks the in-process answer queue. Its single bd show read is issued through the workflow command() seam and blocks at the engine pause gate (_pauseGate in packages/apra-fleet-workflow/src/workflow/index.mjs command(), ~1563-1575), so an answer recorded out of process with bd human respond is never seen and the run stays parked with members reserved (violates owner decision 5 on the 1bsy epic). Operator decision: option (a), a light read poll.

Why this is premium: kb_stats coverage 0.25 across {holdUntilReleased, seedFromLegacy, checkMutatingRequest, sendJson}; holdUntilReleased itself has no KB entry. Cross-package change (generic workflow engine plus fleet-sprint).

Known constraints (from CONFIRMED KB entries, copy verbatim):
- recordDecisionAnswer only queues; mid-run answers apply inside a runner sync bracket via applyRecordedAnswers; it never awaits resume or pushes.
- The needs_decision pause keeps member reservations; cli.mjs wirePauseReservations skips releaseForPause for source needs_decision, and the pre-resume hook runs re-reserve and resync only after a pause that actually released.

Design direction (doer may refine, but the constraints are firm):
1. The poll read targets the backlog member (deps.member in createDecisionWait is runner.js backlogMember: the supervisor-owned, LLM-less, unreservable local member on the project beads folder; see src/supervisor/backlog-member.mjs header). Reading it does not touch any reserved sprint member.
2. Add a narrowly scoped way for this one read to run while the run is paused, without passing the pause gate and without counting as an in-flight activity that would affect pause engagement (e.g. an opts flag on command() honoured by the engine, or a separate pause-exempt read seam injected into createDecisionWait). Keep the workflow package generic (no fleet-sprint or bead terms in the engine API; see docs/generic-engine-boundary.md).
3. Poll cadence: a bd show --json of the holding decision beads every 5 minutes (new constant, overridable via an env var in the same style as APRA_FLEET_DECISION_POLL_MS; the existing 60s in-process queue check stays). No pullBeads/resync, no member release, no requestPause/requestResume per poll; read failures log once per distinct error and the wait keeps going. When a holding decision bead reads closed, requestResume once and apply it through the existing closedAnswers / applyAnswer(via bd human respond, respond:false) path so bead state is identical to today.
4. A stop during a poll read still rejects at once with CancelledError (existing untilStopped behaviour).
5. Update the operator-facing text: the paused log line in awaitAnswer (~563) and the notification line in packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/decision-notify.mjs (~159) must no longer tell the operator to press Resume after bd human respond; they say the answer is picked up within the poll interval. Update the decision-wait.mjs header comment (ANSWER SOURCES paragraph says this is NOT polled) and any doc that repeats it (search docs/ and packages/apra-fleet-se/docs for press Resume / bd human respond).

Expected files (best-effort, not an allowlist): packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/decision-wait.mjs, packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js (wiring), packages/apra-fleet-workflow/src/workflow/index.mjs (pause-exempt read), packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/decision-notify.mjs, packages/apra-fleet-se/test/decision-wait-long-wait.test.mjs and decision-notify.test.mjs (update expectations), docs as found.
beads.acceptance_criteria:
1. While paused awaiting a decision, an answer recorded out of process (the decision bead closed with a Response comment) is detected by a periodic read and the run resumes and applies it, without a dashboard Resume.
2. The poll read runs against the backlog member only. It issues no member release, no re-reserve or resync, no beads pull and no pause/resume per poll. A fake-timer unit test over many intervals asserts the exact command list: only bd show reads at the 5-minute cadence, plus the bd comments read once the bead is closed.
3. The read cadence defaults to 5 minutes and can be overridden by a documented env var. The 60s in-process queue check is unchanged.
4. An operator stop during the wait still rejects at once with CancelledError and runs no further command.
5. The workflow engine change is generic (no fleet-sprint terms), and a paused run still blocks ordinary command() and agent() calls at the pause gate (an existing or new workflow test asserts it).
6. Neither the awaitAnswer pause log line nor the decision-notify message text tells the operator to press Resume. The decision-notify tests assert the new text.
7. npm test passes in packages/apra-fleet-se and packages/apra-fleet-workflow, including the generic-boundary guard.

beads.title: Grant the late-decision extra cycle only for waits at Cycle Evaluation
beads.description: packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js throwIfSetAsideStall adds awaitAnswer results to lateDecisionAnswers whenever cycle >= effectiveMaxCycles, whatever `where` is. A wait at the start of a develop round in the last cycle (runner.js:3534, where = 'start of Develop C<n> R<m>') dispatches the released bead in that same cycle. Even so, handleLateDecisionAnswers still grants an extra cycle past maxCycles if other beads remain open. docs/fleet-sprint-set-aside.md says such waits dispatch the bead in the same cycle and so should not count as late. Only queue late answers from the Cycle Evaluation stall site, and add a mock-sprint test with maxCycles 1 where the decision parks at the start of develop round 2 and other work stays open: it should get no 'granting one extra cycle' log line.
